metadata.title: Delta: Inside the Godot Code
metadata.audience: makers following the channel's Claude + Walker game workflows
metadata.note: godot-gamedev walker film. Code panels are Godot editor reconstructions with verbatim source; each is followed by real engine output of the same build. No game change, no paid calls, no upload.

beats.narration_text: Hola, this is Liam, in for Bear. That's the kind of prompt Walker expects, reconstructed here, not a transcript. This time we open the project itself: a piece of code, then the exact thing it does on screen, in the real build.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about a first-person puzzle game — a space station folded into two layers, energy cells carried between machines, and an unstable core taken past two guardians — into a playable Godot project.
props.runningText: illustrative reconstruction — not the historical prompt
output: Built: 15 thin scenes, 27 scripts and 3 shaders, 5,319 lines.
Art from the Unity folder; levels and sound authored.

beats.narration_text: Delta is built in code. Its twelve level scenes are seven lines each, and fifty-three hundred lines of GDScript and shader code build every wall, device and menu at runtime, from text maps. So every piece of code we read has a result you can watch.

props.text:
Delta
is built from scenes.
Twelve level scenes, seven lines each,
and 5,319 lines of GDScript
that build every level.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant writer: text is typed on screen over the narration, so mid-beat samples legitimately show a partial page. The finished text fills the safe area and holds for the last 1.5 s.

beats.narration_text: Open a level scene and there's one node. Run it for eight seconds, and level dot g d has built the rest: an environment and a sun, an items node with the cell, Upper Delta with its walls, lamps, socket and door, the HUD, and the player with a camera. Six hundred and four nodes.

beats.narration_text: All player input lands here. Mouse motion turns the view, but only while the mouse is captured. Then the actions: jump, E for interact, F for pickup, and Q to switch dimension.

props.title: Look Needs a Captured Mouse

beats.narration_text: F drops whatever you're already holding. Otherwise it asks the ray what's under the crosshair. If it's an item inside a device, it tells you to use E instead. If not, the item is picked up, and the level hears an event.

props.title: Pickup Is a Ray
props.code:
func try_pickup() -> void:
	if held:
		var item := held
		item.drop()
		Audio.play("drop")
		level.emit_event("drop:%s" % item.kind)
		return
	var target := look_target()
	if target.has("pickable"):
		var item: Pickable = target.pickable
		if item.has_holder() and not item.held_by_player():
			# Items in devices come out with [E]
			level.hud.toast(GameState.prompt("Press [] to take it out"))
			return
		item.pickup(self)
		Audio.play("pickup")
		level.emit_event("pickup:%s" % item.kind)

notes.label: In a device
notes.value: comes out with E, not F

beats.narration_text: So the cell is picked up only when the crosshair is on it, and then it floats in front of the camera.

beats.narration_text: Where a shift lands is decided here. It looks at the other layer. If that cell has no floor and no platform, it refuses. Otherwise it tests a player-sized capsule fifty metres away, and if anything solid overlaps it, it refuses again. Unity's switcher had no such check.

props.title: A Shift Can Be Refused

notes.label: Refused
notes.value: no floor, or the capsule overlaps rock

beats.narration_text: So in a corner where Lower Delta has no floor, Q only gives a toast: something solid is in the way.

beats.narration_text: At the peak of the glitch, the shift happens. Unless you're holding the core: then you take damage, it's thrown out of your hands, and it goes critical. Otherwise you move to the target, and whatever you hold moves with you.

props.title: Never Shift Holding the Core
props.code:
func _at_glitch_peak() -> void:
	if final_stage:
		final_stage = false
		level.arrive_final_stage()
		return
	if held and held.kind == "core":
		# Damage() + ExplodeHeldObject(): eject at 50 m/s toward the camera's forward.
		damage()
		var item := held
		item.drop()
		item.linear_velocity = -camera.global_basis.z * 14.0
		item.enter_critical_state()
		return
	var target: Vector3 = level.switch_target(global_position)
	if target == Vector3.INF:
		Audio.play("switch_denied")
		level.hud.toast("Something solid is in the way on the other side")
		return
	var offset := target - global_position
	global_position = target
	velocity.y = 0.0
	_vertical = -2.0
	if held:
		held.global_position += offset
	level.on_switched()

beats.narration_text: Shift with the core: the damage flash, the core flies, explodes, and rebuilds itself at its spawn.

beats.narration_text: The duplicator's button refuses an empty cradle, and it won't copy a copy. If an earlier copy exists, that one is removed first. Then it makes the new copy beside the cradle, with a purple flash.

props.title: Only One Copy
props.code:
func activate() -> void:
	if held == null:
		level.hud.toast("The duplicator is empty")
		return
	if held == last_clone:
		level.hud.toast("It won't copy a copy")
		return
	if last_clone != null and is_instance_valid(last_clone):
		last_clone.drop()
		level.spawn_flash(last_clone.global_position, Color(0.7, 0.45, 1.0))
		last_clone.queue_free()
	last_clone = held.make_clone(clone_point.global_position)
	level.spawn_flash(clone_point.global_position, Color(0.7, 0.45, 1.0))
	Audio.play_at("duplicate", clone_point.global_position, self)
	_flash = 1.0
	emit_event("clone")

notes.label: Refuses
notes.value: empty cradle · a copy of a copy

beats.narration_text: The button pressed with the cell in the cradle: the flash, and a second cell beside it.

beats.narration_text: A strike is a timer. For five seconds the sparks are attached to the player. Then they're moved into the world where they are, and locked, with a red ring of the strike radius. Three seconds later, the lightning hits that spot.

props.title: Follow, Lock, Strike
props.code:
func _update_strike(delta: float) -> void:
	if spark == null:
		return
	spark_timer += delta
	if not spark_locked:
		if spark_timer >= SPARKS_FOLLOWING_DURATION:
			spark_timer = 0.0
			spark_locked = true
			var where := spark.global_position
			spark.get_parent().remove_child(spark)
			level.add_child(spark)
			spark.global_position = where
			Audio.play_at("spark_lock", where, level)
			spark_ring = MeshInstance3D.new()
			var torus := TorusMesh.new()
			torus.inner_radius = STRIKE_RADIUS - 0.15
			torus.outer_radius = STRIKE_RADIUS
			spark_ring.mesh = torus
			spark_ring.scale = Vector3(1, 0.15, 1)
			spark_ring.material_override = Kit.glow(Color(1.0, 0.3, 0.3), 5.0)
			level.add_child(spark_ring)
			spark_ring.global_position = where + Vector3(0, 0.05, 0)
			level.hud.show_warning("STRIKE LOCKED - GET CLEAR")
	elif spark_timer >= SPARKS_LOCK_DURATION:
		var target := spark.global_position
		_cancel_strike()
		_strike(spark_dim, target)
	elif spark_ring:
		spark_ring.visible = fmod(spark_timer, 0.3) < 0.2

notes.label: Follow
notes.value: 5 s, the sparks ride on the player

beats.narration_text: The guardian has found you: the sparks follow, lock, the warning says get clear, and the script does.

beats.narration_text: The same strike is how the level is solved. If the shield generator stands within three metres of where the lightning lands, the shield is destroyed. And if the player is within three metres, the player dies.

props.title: The Strike Is the Key

notes.label: Player

beats.narration_text: So the script waits beside the shield generator until a strike locks there, then steps clear. The shield goes down.

beats.narration_text: Here's the first defect. The pause menu is built, and then the options panel is wrapped in a full-screen centre container, added last. Even with the options hidden, that container covers the whole screen, on top of the pause buttons, and catches every click.

props.title: An Invisible Wall Over the Buttons
props.code:
options = OptionsPanel.new()
	options.visible = false
	var options_center := CenterContainer.new()
	options_center.set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)
	options_center.add_child(options)
	pause_menu.add_child(options_center)

beats.narration_text: So a mouse click on Resume does nothing. Only the arrow keys and Enter reach the menu.

beats.narration_text: And the second. The level's input handler toggles pause on Escape, and while paused, R restarts and N skips. But this node pauses with the rest of the tree, so once the game is paused, it never receives another key. Escape won't resume, and R and N do nothing.

props.title: Keys a Paused Node Never Hears

notes.value: the level pauses with the tree

beats.narration_text: R, pressed while paused: nothing. The menu's own Restart level, chosen with the keys, works.

beats.narration_text: The rest of the project, in one pass. A main menu with Continue, Select level and options, a How to play page, and credits. An audio autoload with synthesized sounds and music. A kit autoload for the models. Tools that convert the Unity art, and a playtest that steers through a hook in the player script. The film's captures pressed the keys instead.

beats.narration_text: Verdict. This is a project you can read top to bottom: thin scenes, levels as text, one small script per device. Two real defects live in the pause menu: a container that eats clicks, and a handler that pauses itself. The game's own test never paused, so it never saw them. And nobody has played it yet.

artifactLines: Implemented: 15 thin scenes; level.gd builds each level from an ASCII map.
Good habits: shift refusal; a core that rebuilds; one copy at a time.
Defects: hud.gd:316 container eats clicks; level.gd:804 never runs while paused.
Not judged: fun, difficulty, level 12 fairness. 0 human playtests.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude in your own Godot project: Use Walker on my Godot project. Find one input handler that is supposed to work while the game is paused. Predict whether it will ever run. Then write a capture that pauses with real input, presses the key, and checks what happened, and only after that, propose the smallest fix. Liam, in for Bear.
